variables.systemDescription: The SNES-MSU1 is an enhancement for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES enabling high-quality audio and video playback through a custom chip. The development stems from the fallout of Nintendo's partnership with Sony in 1991, when Nintendo chose to collaborate with Philips instead, canceling the SNES CD-ROM project. Sony would go on to make history with the Playstation. In the early 2010s, enthusiasts created the MSU1 (Multi-Sample Unit 1) to expand the SNES's limited audio and storage capabilities. Developers created homebrew games and patches to utilize the MSU1 for CD-quality music and larger game sizes. This innovation revitalized interest in classic SNES (and NES!) titles and showcased the potential for retro gaming enhancements, leading to a resurgence of fan-made projects and a deeper appreciation for the SNES's legacy.
